challenges.issue: The causal chain's critical hop — that the expired certificate is OUR client credential and not a partner-side trust/expiry change — rests on a single application log line (F8). The log is written by payment-service interpreting a TLS alert; alert 45 is generated by the receiving peer about the cert it rejected, but no finding shows the partner's handshake view or any second, independent source (cert store, secret manager, second caller). The assumption is explicitly listed and unverified. Severity: major, not blocking, because onset, scope and metrics all independently corroborate an outbound mTLS rejection on our path, and the internal 100%-failure scope makes a pure partner outage less likely (a partner outage would typically not produce identical instant onset tied to our notAfter).

H2 was rejected essentially by precedent inference (F14/F15/F18) and by the wording of our own log, not by any direct observation of the partner side (telemetry disabled, F3). It is not formally 'contradicted' — the contradicting list cites F8/F7, which are the same evidence being interpreted. If the expired cert belonged to the partner, remediation differs entirely (wait/failover vs. reissue). A single check that the cert binding present in payment-service's own certificate store/secret has notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z would collapse or confirm this.

Blast radius is unconfirmed: nothing establishes whether the failed credential is per-service (only payment-service's own client cert) or shared across all callers of bank-partner-api. F9's bank_api_error_rate is reported for payment-service only; no metric was pulled for settlement-service/order-service, which share ledger-db/kafka but whose bank-call usage is unverified. If other services calling bank-partner-api also hit 100% at 12:15Z, the fault is a shared credential (different owner and fix scope) rather than a payment-service-specific expiry.

The 'no earlier error exists' claim (F7) rests on a narrow 11:30–12:16 query plus one 11:00–13:59 query, and the change feeds returned nothing between 2026-04-01T00:00Z and 10:30Z (change-feed coverage gap). Absence of a cert-renewal attempt or truststore/egress change in that period is therefore not established, so an earlier renewal failure that triggered the expiry cannot be excluded.

F12's latency evidence compares p99 only (latency_p95_ms query failed, not_found) and db_pool_in_use; it is still adequate to rule out timeout/pool mechanisms for the rejected calls, but the p95-based 'no latency impact' statement is thinner than presented. Minor, does not affect the origin.

critiques.summary: H1 is now adequately grounded and H2 is contradicted rather than merely dismissed. My round-1 blocking issue — "is the expired cert ours or the partner's?" — is resolved by evidence, not by the app's self-report alone: (a) F30 shows an independent local cert-watcher already naming CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal with notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z at 11:50:26Z, 25 min BEFORE expiry and before any failure, so the notAfter is not a post-hoc rationalization in the error log; (b) F29/F28 establish the failure direction is 'remote sent alert 45 against our client cert' with no peer CN, no trust-anchor and no hostname-mismatch string anywhere, whereas the H2 precedent class (HIST-103/HIST-105, F14/F18) presents as partner 5xx/504/timeouts — none of which appear; (c) F19/F20 show no credential/egress/auth change and no relevant deployment in 7 days, so a partner-side or internal trust change has no footprint; (d) F21/F22 establish the bank-partner-api edge is external, non-shared and reachable only from payment-service, and F25/F27 show no other service exposes the metric or a cert symptom (settlement-service error_rate flat, zero cert logs). Timing is tight: cert expiry 12:15:00Z, first failure 12:15:27Z, bank_api_error_rate 0.20%->100%, success 99.17%->~2% (F7-F10). Alternatives are contradicted on mechanism (TLS alert 45, not timeouts/contention) and timing (55-min and 105-min quiet gaps for cfg-2502/dep-5510), and F12 excludes latency/pool saturation. Residual gaps (other services' metrics unread due to budget, no secret-store read, no cron view, partner telemetry off) are secondary detail that does not change the origin or the fix — a reissue of a payment-service-scoped credential — so they warrant a confidence cap, not another round.

challenges.issue: notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z and its payment-service-only binding are never read from an authoritative secret/cert-store record; they rest on the application's own TLS log (F8) plus the local cert-watcher copy of the same value (F30) and an inference from the dependency graph (F21/F22). Corroborated by three independent artifacts, but still not first-hand.

Latent cause 'renewal automation failed/absent' has no scheduler/cron evidence — F23 is a HIST-106 precedent only. The fix (reissue) is unaffected, but the 'why it lapsed' framing is asserted, not shown.

Blast radius is only confirmed for payment-service (failing) and settlement-service (clean, F26/F27); order-, portfolio- and notification-service metrics/logs were never read (budget exhausted). The external/non-shared edge and F25 make a wider blast radius implausible, but it is inferred rather than measured.

Not positively excluded by partner-side telemetry (has_telemetry:false); it is disfavoured by negative evidence (no peer CN, no trust-anchor/hostname error, no partner 5xx/504/timeout signature) and by the independent pre-expiry cert-watcher line. Disfavoured is sufficient here, but it is not a hard refutation.
